songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Acoustic first set shines; electric third delivers fiery Viola Lee
ai_show_review.blurb: The show opens with tight acoustic numbers and builds into a powerful electric third set highlighted by a scorching Viola Lee Blues and high‑energy Lovelight. Jerry’s guitar work is solid throughout, Phil stays on key, while Pigpen’s organ sits low in the mix. Standout moments include Casey Jones, the Good Lovin’/Not Fade Away sequence and the closing And We Bid You Good Night.
ai_show_review.review:
On March 20, 1970 at the Capitol Theater the Dead delivered a set that balances folk‑tightness with electric fire. The first acoustic half works like a well‑crafted songbook—Casey Jones rolls into Me And My Uncle, and the China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue feels fresh, while Deep Elem Blues and Friend Of The Devil showcase earnest storytelling. After a modest dip on Hard To Handle, the band erupts in the third set: a blistering Viola Lee Blues, soaring High Time, and an exuberant Turn On Your Lovelight keep the momentum high. The Good Lovin’ → Not Fade Away double‑drum stretch is a highlight of dual percussion energy, culminating in a heartfelt And We Bid You Good Night encore.

The recordings capture this performance with varying fidelity. The Smith soundboard (gd1970-03-20.sbd.smith.99182.sbeok.flac16) offers the clearest overall picture—though some tape hiss and a low‑mix organ keep it from being pristine, it still presents the acoustic nuances and the fiery electric moments vividly. Other SBD sources are good but uneven, while the matrix splice is jumbled and muffled in places. For most listeners the Smith SBD is the definitive listening experience.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: All three recordings are marked as mixed sentiment. Reviewers consistently praise specific songs (Viola Lee Blues, Good Lovin’, etc.) and note no pervasive negative criticism of the band's playing, resulting in a modest positive adjustment rather than a strong one.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality soundboard with decent clarity; captures acoustic set and fiery electric moments despite minor hiss and low organ level.

key_highlights: Acoustic first set shines with tight folk numbers.
Scorching Viola Lee Blues and high‑energy Turn On Your Lovelight in the third set.
Epic Good Lovin’ → Not Fade Away double‑drum sequence and powerful And We Bid You Good Night encore.
Soundboard recording is good but has some tape hiss and low organ mix.
song_highlights: And We Bid You Good Night

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers confident lead lines and an inspired solo during Viola Lee Blues, keeping the electric momentum driving.
band_performance.Phil: Sings loudly and stays on key throughout, providing solid vocal support.
band_performance.Brent: Pigpen’s organ sits low in the mix, reducing its impact especially on Viola Lee Blues.

must_listen_sequences: And We Bid You Good Night
